item.title: “Migajāla, there are phenomena cognizable by the mind that are desirable … enticing. If a monk does not delight in them, does not praise them,…
item.description:
“Migajāla, there are phenomena cognizable by the mind that are desirable … enticing. If a monk does not delight in them, does not praise them, and dwells without lust for them, then delight ceases. With the cessation of delight, lust ceases. With the cessation of lust, bondage ceases. Not being bound by the bondage of delight, Migajāla, that monk is called ‘one who dwells alone.’ Even if he lives in the midst of a village crowded with monks, nuns, laymen, laywomen, kings, royal ministers, ascetics of other sects and their disciples — still he is called ‘one who dwells alone.’ Why? Because craving, the companion, has been abandoned by him. Therefore he is called ‘one who dwells alone.’”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.63
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: Sitting down to one side, those monks said to the Blessed One: - Here, venerable sir, King Pasenadi of Kosala has had many people bound.…
item.description:
Sitting down to one side, those monks said to the Blessed One:
- Here, venerable sir, King Pasenadi of Kosala has had many people bound. Some are bound with ropes, some with chains, some with shackles.

Then the Blessed One, understanding the meaning of this, on that occasion recited this verse:
The wise say that such binding
Is not strong —
Binding with iron, with ropes,
With wooden shackles —
But infatuation with sensual pleasures,
With jewels and ornaments,
And anxious thoughts
Directed toward children and wives —
The wise say this binding
Is truly strong.
Though it drags one down,
Subtle and hard to escape,
True renunciants cut it in two,
Without wishing or longing,
Abandoning all sensual pleasures.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 3.10
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Ānanda, those noble thoughts that are conducive to progress and lead to the complete destruction of suffering — such as renunciation thoughts, non-ill-will thoughts, harmlessness…
item.description:
“Ānanda, those noble thoughts that are conducive to progress and lead to the complete destruction of suffering — such as renunciation thoughts, non-ill-will thoughts, harmlessness thoughts — he reflects: ‘I will think these thoughts.’ In this way, he is clearly aware of that.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 122 – Mahāsuññatasutta
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “I do not see any other thing, monks, that so prevents unarisen sensual desire from arising, or abandons arisen sensual desire, as the sign of…
item.description:
“I do not see any other thing, monks, that so prevents unarisen sensual desire from arising, or abandons arisen sensual desire, as the sign of the foul. The sign of the foul, monks, when wisely attended to, prevents unarisen sensual desire from arising and abandons arisen sensual desire.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 1.16
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Then, while the Venerable Udāyi was in solitary retreat, this thought arose in his mind: ‘Indeed, the Blessed One has abandoned many painful states for…
item.description:
“Then, while the Venerable Udāyi was in solitary retreat, this thought arose in his mind: ‘Indeed, the Blessed One has abandoned many painful states for us. Indeed, the Blessed One has brought us many pleasant states. Indeed, the Blessed One has abandoned many unwholesome states for us. Indeed, the Blessed One has brought us many wholesome states.’”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 66 – Laṭukikopamasutta
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: Elder Nandaka: Foul is the thing! Full of foul smell and stench, Possessed by Māra, Oozing many streams — This body has nine streams, Always…
item.description:
Elder Nandaka:

Foul is the thing!
Full of foul smell and stench,
Possessed by Māra,
Oozing many streams —
This body has nine streams,
Always flowing.

Do not despise the ancients!
Do not insult the Tathāgata!
They do not long for the heavenly realm,
Let alone the human world.

The fool, without wisdom,
With evil intent, enveloped by delusion —
That one, full of lust,
Is caught in Māra’s snare.

Those who have escaped
Greed, hatred, and delusion —
They are not lustful,
The snare is cut, they are unbound.

From: Theragāthā 4.4
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, defilement is a disease; defilement is a boil; defilement is a dart. Therefore, monks, the Tathāgata dwells without defilement, free from the dart. Therefore,…
item.description:
“Monks, defilement is a disease; defilement is a boil; defilement is a dart. Therefore, monks, the Tathāgata dwells without defilement, free from the dart. Therefore, monks, if any monk has a wish, let him wish to dwell without defilement, free from the dart. Do not conceive about the eye, do not conceive in the eye, do not conceive from the eye, do not conceive ‘the eye is mine.’ Do not conceive about forms … Do not conceive about eye-consciousness … Do not conceive about eye-contact … Whatever feeling arises dependent on eye-contact … do not conceive about that feeling, do not conceive in it, do not conceive from it, do not conceive ‘that feeling is mine.’ Do not conceive about everything, do not conceive in everything, do not conceive from everything, do not conceive ‘everything is mine.’ Not conceiving thus, he does not cling to anything in the world. Not clinging, he is not agitated. Not agitated, he personally attains Nibbāna. He knows: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more of this state of being.’”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.90
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Rādha, whatever desire, lust, delight, craving there is for form — abandon it. Thus that form will be abandoned, cut off at the root, made…
item.description:
“Rādha, whatever desire, lust, delight, craving there is for form — abandon it. Thus that form will be abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, made non-existent, so that it cannot arise again in the future. Regarding feeling … perception … formations … Rādha, whatever desire, lust, delight, craving there is for consciousness — abandon it. Thus that consciousness will be abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, made non-existent, so that it cannot arise again in the future.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 23.9
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, then I dwelt heedful, ardent, resolute. When a sensual thought arose, I understood: ‘This sensual thought has arisen in me, and it leads to…
item.description:
“Monks, then I dwelt heedful, ardent, resolute. When a sensual thought arose, I understood: ‘This sensual thought has arisen in me, and it leads to my own harm, to others’ harm, to the harm of both, destroys wisdom, is part of vexation, does not lead to Nibbāna.’ Monks, as I reflected: ‘This sensual thought leads to my own harm’ – it subsided. As I reflected: ‘It leads to others’ harm’ – it subsided. As I reflected: ‘It leads to the harm of both’ – it subsided. As I reflected: ‘It destroys wisdom, is part of vexation, does not lead to Nibbāna’ – it subsided. Thus, monks, I continued to remove, abandon, and put an end to sensual thoughts.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 19 – Dvedhāvitakkasutta
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “He understands thus: ‘Previously I had greed — that was unwholesome. Now I have none. Thus it is wholesome. Previously I had hatred — that…
item.description:
“He understands thus: ‘Previously I had greed — that was unwholesome. Now I have none. Thus it is wholesome. Previously I had hatred — that was unwholesome. Now I have none. Thus it is wholesome. Previously I had delusion — that was unwholesome. Now I have none. Thus it is wholesome.’ Thus, in this very life, he is freed from longing, calm, cooled, experiencing ease, abiding in the Brahma-state himself.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 3.66
📖 Read this sutta
